title: Local profiles silently replaced wholesale by a stale/unrelated Nightscout profile document (no merge, no confirmation)
body:
# Title
Local profiles silently replaced wholesale by a stale/unrelated Nightscout profile document (no merge, no confirmation)

# Body

## Summary

`ProfilePlugin.loadFromStore()` (and its successor `ProfileRepositoryImpl.loadFromStoreInternal()` in the
in-progress "reactive profile store" rework) unconditionally **replaces the entire local profile list**
with whatever profile document NS considers "current", as soon as `NsIncomingDataProcessor.processProfile()`
decides to accept it. There is no merge, no diff shown to the user, and no confirmation dialog — a locally
curated set of profiles can be silently reduced to a single throwaway/test profile the instant NS's profile
collection produces a document with a newer timestamp than the device's `LocalProfileLastChange` watermark.

This is not limited to "Full Sync" — it happens on **ordinary background sync** too, as long as
"Accept NS profile store" is enabled (or `AAPSCLIENT`/follower mode, which always accepts it).

## Steps to reproduce (confirmed from device logs)

1. Device has several local profiles (7, in the log we captured) synced with Nightscout, `LocalProfileLastChange`
   pointing at whichever profile store was last accepted.
2. At some later point, Nightscout's `profile` collection gets a **newer** document — in our case simply named
   `"New profile"` with generic default values (looked like something created/tested in the NS web Profile Editor,
   or a stray write from another client). This does not require any explicit sync action by the user.
3. On the next normal sync poll (`LoadProfileStoreWorker` in NSClientV3), the app fetches this NS document,
   evaluates `createdAt (of NS doc) > lastLocalChange` → true (simply because it's chronologically newer,
   regardless of content/relevance) → calls `loadFromStore()`.
4. `loadFromStore()` validates each profile inside the incoming store; if at least one passes validation, it does:
   ```kotlin
   profiles = newProfiles   // ProfilePlugin.kt:265 (same in ProfileRepositoryImpl.loadFromStoreInternal)
   ```
   replacing the **entire** previous local list.
5. Result: all 7 previously-configured local profiles are gone, replaced by the single generic "New profile".
   No dialog, no warning beyond a debug log line (`Accepted N profiles`).

## Log evidence (timestamps/values from a real device log, profile names anonymized)

```
04.07 02:17:38  Received profileStore: createdAt: 1783120575477  Local last modification: 1783103978893
                Accepted 7 profiles                     # local set becomes a 7-profile store "A"

05.07 23:45:18  Received profileStore: createdAt: 1783283998725  Local last modification: 1783120575477
                Accepted 1 profiles                     # ALL 7 profiles replaced by a single generic profile "B"
                                                         # (Δ ~45h newer, no mod-1000 heuristic involved — genuinely
                                                         #  "newer" by clock, but NOT what the user wanted active)

06.07 00:05:46  Received profileStore: createdAt: 1783285521578  Local last modification: 1783283998725
                Accepted 1 profiles                     # same content, just a metadata bump

06.07 00:48:10  Received profileStore: createdAt: 1783287332568  Local last modification: 1783285521578
                Accepted 1 profiles                     # replaced again, by yet another single-profile document
```

No `Full sync is requested` appears near any of these — all four replacements happened during **normal**
background sync polling.

## Root cause

- `NsIncomingDataProcessor.processProfile()`:
  ```kotlin
  if (createdAt > lastLocalChange || createdAt % 1000 == 0L) { // whole second means edited in NS
      profileSource.loadFromStore(store)
  ```
  Accepts *any* chronologically-newer NS profile store unconditionally — there's no check that the incoming
  store is actually a superset/reasonable evolution of the current local set. The `createdAt % 1000 == 0L`
  branch ("whole second means edited in NS") is additionally very permissive, since most NS profile documents
  (web-UI edits, imports, seed/default profiles) have zero sub-second precision in `created_at`/`startDate`.

- `ProfilePlugin.loadFromStore()` / `ProfileRepositoryImpl.loadFromStoreInternal()`:
  ```kotlin
  profiles = newProfiles
  ```
  Wholesale replace, no merge with existing local profiles, no user confirmation. Confirmed this is
  unchanged in the current in-progress "reactive profile store" rework — the new code even has a comment
  explicitly acknowledging the full-list replacement is intentional, so this looks like a deliberate
  design choice rather than an oversight — but the combination with the very permissive accept-gate above
  produces a genuinely destructive UX for anyone who keeps multiple curated local profiles and also has
  "Accept NS profile store" enabled (or uses AAPSCLIENT/follower mode, where it's always on).

## Suggested directions (not prescriptive — flagging for maintainer input)

- Merge incoming NS profiles into the local list by name instead of wholesale replacing, OR
- Require explicit user confirmation (with a diff: "N local profiles → M from NS") before applying an
  NS-driven profile store change outside of an explicit "Import"/"Full Sync" user action, OR
- At minimum, tighten the `createdAt % 1000 == 0L` heuristic, since it accepts almost any NS document
  regardless of actual relative recency.

## Environment
- AndroidAPS fork based on 4.0/beta-3.4.2.3-apex lineage (NSClientV3)
- Also confirmed present in latest `dev`/`master` as of the May 2026 "reactive profile store" rework
  (`ProfileRepositoryImpl.kt`)

comments.body:
Full disclosure: the analysis above (code exploration, root-cause tracing through `NsIncomingDataProcessor`/`ProfilePlugin`/`ProfileRepositoryImpl`, and the device-log evidence) was produced with AI assistance (Claude Code) — I described the symptom and supplied the logs, and the assistant did the digging, which I then reviewed.

No PR has been opened for this issue. Per `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s AI contribution policy, I'm keeping this as analysis/context only and leaving the actual fix (if one is wanted) to a maintainer — flagging the AI involvement proactively rather than leaving it unstated.

This is hard to achieve because sync is done on backround (no questions possible)
Anyway, editing profile in NS is not recommended and in v4 not enabled by default becauce NS allows to create profile which is invalid in AAPS.
New master-client solves editing profiles as one atomic operation with fast syncing so brick level sync is not necessary
